note: Gate spec for the shared paste-enforcement Stop hook (hooks/paste-gate.py in the
agent-skills repo, installed as ~/.claude/hooks/paste-gate.py). The engine, the
failure it guards against and the detection rules are documented there.
`threads.py sync` is deliberately NOT gated even though the "status-only" doc path
pastes its output too: the opener also runs `sync` as silent,
intentionally-unshown prep (identical command text), so gating it would false-block
every opener turn demanding a redundant paste of that silent prep call. `todo` has no
such double-duty — it's only ever the user-facing status answer — so it's safe.

gates.reason: You ran `threads.py present` (the opener) but your message did not include its output. Tool output is COLLAPSED — the user cannot see it. Re-send your message starting with the FULL `present` output pasted verbatim: the MR title line, the overview table, and (if there is one) the first open topic's block — the fenced code the comment is anchored to, then the blockquoted comment. Do not summarise it or lead with your own research prose.
You ran `threads.py todo` for a status-only request but your message did not include its output. Re-send your message with the FULL table pasted verbatim, not a paraphrase.

You ran `threads.py quote` (moving to the next topic) but your message did not include its output. Re-send your message starting with the FULL quote block pasted verbatim: the topic header, the fenced code the comment is anchored to, and the reviewer's blockquoted note with every reply. Not your own research prose, and not the note without the code — the user cannot judge a comment about lines they were never shown.

You ran `diff-view.sh` to show this topic's working diff but your message did not include its output. Re-send your message with the FULL diff-view block pasted verbatim — the fenced diff and the final 'ACK to fix up and push?' — before asking for that ACK any other way. Never commit, push, or ask for the ACK without the diff actually shown.

note: The signature is the draft LABEL's prefix, not `**Draft reply:**`, because the
command has two renders: the full block for a topic's first reply, and
`--refine` for a reworded draft on a topic already on screen, which labels the
draft `**Draft reply — ◈ t4:**` and drops the code and thread. Pinning the
colon would leave the refine render ungated — the one the model is most likely
to drop, since it is the short one.
gates.reason: You ran `threads.py reply-view` for this reply but your message did not include its output. Tool output is COLLAPSED — the user cannot see it. Re-send your message as the FULL reply-view block pasted verbatim: for a first reply that is the topic header, the fenced code, the reviewer's blockquoted note + every reply, the **Draft reply:** block, the Thread (to post on): URL and the final c/p/n prompt line; with `--refine` it is the draft, the URL and the prompt. Do not summarise it to just the prompt.

You ran `change-view` / `change-preview.sh` to illustrate a trivial topic's fix but your message did not include its output. Re-send your message with the FULL change-preview block pasted verbatim — the fenced illustration and the final 'Agreed?' — not a description of the change.

note: `needs_summary` is derived — a topic here always comes from a reviewer's
thread, so no authored summary means nobody wrote one — and render_table marks
such a row with this exact glyph+label. The row then carries the raw comment,
truncated, which is what the table looked like before this rule: 28 rows of
somebody else's sentence starts, three of them opening with a code fence.
Anchored to a table row (`^\|`) so prose mentioning the phrase cannot trip it.
Mirrors review-mr's unresolved-needs-title-table.
forbidden.reason: Your message pastes an overview table whose Summary column still holds a raw reviewer comment (`✍️ needs summary:`) instead of a title somebody wrote. That column is how the user tells one topic from another, and a truncated German sentence — or a ```suggestion fence — is unreadable there. Read the open threads (`threads.py bodies`) and give each flagged topic a short English line with `threads.py set <t> --summary "…"`, then re-render (`sync`/`todo`/`present`) and send that. (Both MR skills emit this warning and the hook may hand you the other one's wording: the command is `findings.py` in review-mr and `threads.py` in rework-mr — use the one this session's skill ships.)

forbidden.note: Same gap as above, but for `quote`'s / `present`'s topic heading (render_quote's needs_summary_warning) rather than a table row. Mirrors review-mr's unresolved-needs-title-quote.
forbidden.reason: Your message pastes a topic whose heading warns it has no authored `summary` — the heading is the bare topic handle, which tells the user nothing about which point this is. Read the thread and run `threads.py set <t> --summary "<short English line>"`, then re-run `quote <t>` (or `present`) and send that. (Both MR skills emit this warning and the hook may hand you the other one's wording: the command is `findings.py` in review-mr and `threads.py` in rework-mr — use the one this session's skill ships.)

note: `summary_language_warning` emits this exact phrase in the table footer and in a
topic heading whenever an authored summary reads as German. The check is
conservative (function words only, code spans stripped, two distinct hits), so a
message carrying the warning really does have a summary to reword.
Mirrors review-mr's summary-in-draft-language.
forbidden.reason: Your message pastes a view whose warning says one or more summaries are written in the thread's language. A summary is the one-line title the user reads in the table and in every topic heading, and it is English; the thread's language governs one thing only, the body of a reply you post into it. Reword each named topic (`threads.py set <t> --summary "<short English line>"`), re-render, and send that instead. (Both MR skills emit this warning and the hook may hand you the other one's wording: the command is `findings.py` in review-mr and `threads.py` in rework-mr — use the one this session's skill ships.)

note: The inverse of the diff-view gate: that gate only fires once diff-view.sh has RUN,
so skipping the script entirely — asking for the ACK straight out of prose — used to
pass unseen. SKILL.md states it as an absolute: never ask for the ACK without the
diff actually shown. The phrase is the script's own closing line, so a legitimate
message containing it has necessarily pasted diff-view's output (and the gate above
then checks the whole block); a message containing it with no run behind it can only
have written it out itself.
Anchored to a line start (with markdown/blockquote prefixes allowed) so that merely
TALKING about the phrase mid-sentence — editing this skill, quoting SKILL.md — is not
a hit; only presenting it as the ask is.
There is deliberately NO equivalent rule for change-preview's 'Agreed?': the
non-trivial branch ends with a plain discussion question, which can legitimately be
phrased that way, so it would block correct turns.
required.reason: You asked for the fixup+push ACK without running `diff-view.sh`, so the user is being asked to approve a fixup and force-push they cannot see. Run `$SD/diff-view.sh <t>` and re-send your message with its FULL output pasted verbatim — the fenced diff and the script's own closing ACK line — as the last thing in the message. Never commit, push, or ask for the ACK without the diff actually shown.
